o: Explain benefits and drawbacks for different stakeholders.
Write balanced six-mark evaluations using specific evidence.
Reach a justified conclusion about a digital-technology decision.
c: Describe the proposed technology and its context first. A strong evaluation considers different viewpoints, consequences and realistic trade-offs.
Users, employees, managers and the wider community may be affected differently. Give real impacts rather than simply saying technology is good or bad.
Discuss appropriate ethical, legal, environmental, cultural or privacy aspects. Do not force every category into every answer if it is irrelevant.
Make a reasoned decision that recognises the most important benefit and risk in the given scenario. Explain conditions that would make the decision more acceptable.

m.title: Build a balanced six-mark evaluation
m.q: A school plans to use automated facial recognition to record attendance. Evaluate TWO benefits and TWO concerns, then give a supported judgement. [6 marks]
st: Identify the aim: recording attendance quickly and accurately.
Automation may reduce administrative time [1] so staff can focus on teaching [1].
Face data is sensitive personal information and may produce privacy or fairness concerns [1]; inaccurate recognition could affect pupils [1].
A justified judgement [2]: only consider use with lawful safeguards, accuracy checks and a fair non-biometric alternative. Credit reasoned alternative conclusions.

w: A town council plans to replace most paper communications with a mobile app. Evaluate benefits and drawbacks, with a judgement. [6 marks]

An app may speed communication [1] and reduce paper/postage [1]. People without smartphones/digital skills could be excluded [1], harming fair access [1]. A reasoned judgement [2] could support the app if telephone and paper alternatives remain available.
A company allows staff to work remotely using cloud services. Evaluate an advantage and a concern. [4 marks]

Staff can access work from different locations [1], improving flexibility [1]. Cloud access depends on connection/security safeguards [1], so outages or poor access control could disrupt work or expose data [1].
A school installs more computers rather than repairing current ones. Evaluate an environmental and social consequence. [4 marks]

More computers may improve access for students [1], reducing some classroom waiting or sharing [1]. Replacing working machines creates e-waste/material demand [1], increasing environmental impact [1].
wSteps: Consider cost, access and environmental effect.
Faster updates and less paper can benefit the council [2].
Digital exclusion is a risk [2]; conclude with an inclusive approach [2].

k.q: Ask for a technology preference, then display a reason prompt using OCR ERL.
k.code:
choice = input("Prefer online or paper?")
print(choice)
print("Explain your reason")
p: Predict which values are printed when input is online.
Add a print statement reminding the user to consider another viewpoint.
k.a:
If the input is online, the program prints online and Explain your reason.
If the input is paper, it prints paper and Explain your reason.

Evaluate a company's proposal to monitor employee locations with a work app. Consider ethical and privacy effects and reach a judgement. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official OCR past paper.

Location monitoring may help coordinate work or safety [1], giving managers useful scheduling information [1]. It may intrude into employees' privacy [1] or harm trust [1]. A justified conclusion [2] should weigh necessity, lawfulness, transparency, limits and proportionate alternatives.

r: State what a software licence does. [2 marks]
Sets out conditions or permissions for using software [1], including copying/modification/distribution rights [1].
State one action prohibited by the Computer Misuse Act 1990. [1 mark]
What does the Program Counter hold during the fetch-execute cycle? [1 mark]
Address of the next instruction to be fetched [1].
A pupil opens another pupil's school account without permission but does not delete any work. Explain why this can still be computer misuse. [4 marks]
The account contains computer material [1], which the pupil deliberately accessed [1] without permission [1]. Unauthorised access is prohibited even without deleting or modifying data [1].
